note: Portraits chosen by hand, not by Wikidata's P18. Each one was looked at before it was written down here, because nothing else can tell a portrait from a building: searching Commons for these names returns lecture theatres, gravestones, a scan of a 1957 doctoral thesis, the profile of Alfred Nobel on the medal itself, and -- for the item whose English label had been vandalised -- an actor. A filename is not evidence. Every entry below names the file, why it was picked, and what the automatic pass had found instead.

Q131112.why: Close portrait, White House photograph and therefore public domain. Wikidata's P18 pointed at a GFDL 1.2 file, which this site excludes because honouring that licence means reproducing its full text.

Q104668.why: Head-and-shoulders portrait. P18 pointed at a CC SA 1.0 file -- a deprecated share-alike with nothing modern to point a reader at. The category also holds a lecture-theatre shot of him side-on at a blackboard, which is him but is not a portrait.

Q103598.why: Head-and-shoulders, 1995. P18 pointed at a GFDL 1.2 file.

Q106699.why: Royal Society studio portrait. P18 pointed at a GFDL 1.2 file; the category's other candidate is a group photograph with President Bush.

Q70554.why: Signed historical portrait, public domain. P18 pointed at a Wellcome Collection scan that Commons has no small rendition of -- every width returns the original at 396 KB, sixty times the median.

Q233965.why: Signed photograph at his microscope, public domain. P18 pointed at another Wellcome scan with the same no-rendition problem. The category also holds an oil painting of him, which is a likeness but not a photograph.
